title: Regression snapshot and canary comparison — lab notes
content:
Purpose
This is a working lab notebook for the January–February 2025 latency regression we saw on the hosted API (p95 spike ~30% across small-model routes). The goal: capture raw snapshots, sanity-check telemetry, run targeted microbenchmarks, and produce a concise canary-vs-main comparison that will shrink the search space for bisect or remediation.

High-level approach (one-liner)
1) Capture identical workload snapshots (traffic replay) from the time of alert. 2) Collect low-level traces (kernel timings, NVTX spans, eBPF) and runtime counters. 3) Run microbenchmarks with controlled variables (batch size, concurrency, sequence length, kv-warmup). 4) Produce a diff heatmap and prioritized hypothesis list for bisect.

Quick context
- Alert: p95 token-generation latency increased from 340ms -> 440ms on model small-redwood-v1 in us-west1 on 2025-01-07 03:14 UTC.
- Canary rollout: there was a small canary (5%) of a runtime change (batch scheduler tweak, PR 587) active from 2025-01-06 22:00 UTC.
- Affected routes: text-generation.short, chat.delta-lite (both low-latency targets).

What we captured (artifacts to keep):
- Telemetry snapshot: metrics export (prometheus snapshot) for 2025-01-06 21:30 -> 2025-01-07 04:00 UTC (service/host/tagged). File: prom-snapshot-20250107.json stored in infra/backups.
- Flamegraphs and NVTX traces from the two hottest servers (host-41, host-48) collected during the spike window.
- eBPF sbpf tracing output for CPU scheduler latencies (sampled at 100Hz).
- GPU kernel timelines from nvtx/nvprof and the runtime's op-trace.
- Request/response sample payloads (anonymized) for failed/slower requests.

Checklist — first 90 minutes
- [x] Pin a clean copy of production config (model version, batch settings, perf flags) for main and canary.
- [x] Export host-level metrics: CPU, IO, GPU util, PCIe memcopy rates, thread-steal, page faults.
- [x] Pull the canary commit diff (PR 587) and annotate what changed: scheduler loop + micro-optimizations in batch coalescer.
- [x] Reproduce locally with replay driver (replay --start 2025-01-07T02:50Z --end 2025-01-07T03:20Z --scale 1x) on a staging node with identical HW.
- [x] Record p50/p95/p99 and per-token timings during replay.

Raw observations from replay
- Main runtime (pre-change): p95 ~ 348ms, p99 ~ 612ms. CPU resident thread count stable.
- Canary runtime (PR 587): p95 ~ 460ms, p99 ~ 730ms. Notable micro-pattern: an additional 12–18ms variance at token step 0 of generation (first-token overhead) and increased tail during high-concurrency bursts.
- NVTX traces: a 10–20ms increase in time spent inside batch-coalescer spin-wait in canary.
- GPU: SM utilization identical across runs; memory copy time (H2D) slightly increased (~2–3ms) but within noise.

Hypotheses (ranked)
1) Scheduler spin/wait introduced by coalescer change in PR 587 leads to CPU-side stalls that cascade into higher queue build-up and higher tail latency. Evidence: NVTX, stacktraces show more time in coalescer path.
2) Interaction with small-batch warmup: canary increases lock contention when batches are below target size leading to more frequent wakeups. Evidence: higher syscall wakeups per second in perf samples.
3) Noisy neighbor / host-level interference coincidental with rollout. Evidence against: replay on isolated staging reproduced delta.
4) Subtle change in batching heuristics caused earlier flushing of batches at cold start (first-token overhead). Evidence: first-token overhead increase.

Microbench suite (commands to run)
- Replay: ./tools/replay --snapshot prom-snapshot-20250107.json --routes text-generation.short --concurrency 8 --scale 1 --out logs/replay-canary.log
- Instrumented run: LD_PRELOAD=./libtrace.so ./runtime --nvtx --tracing=op-trace --config canary-config.yaml > logs/trace.txt 2>&1
- eBPF CPU: sudo ./scripts/capture-sched-latency.sh --pid <runtime-pid> --out ebpf-host41.txt
- GPU kernel timeline: nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt -o nsight-canary host-48-run

Diff analysis plan
- Produce per-span latency histograms (first-token, KV-load, forward, postprocess) and compute delta histograms (canary-main).
- Create heatmap of p95 deltas by route x host x hour (small matrix).
- Compute per-batch-size deltas (1,2,4,8,16). If delta grows at small batch sizes, bias to hypothesis #2.

Interpretation rules (how to decide next step)
- If canary shows consistent extra wall-time inside batch scheduler path across multiple hosts and in isolated replay -> revert the change and open a rollback.
- If discrepancy only at extremely high concurrency not observed in normal traffic -> set guardrails (throttle) and continue iterating.
- If delta reproduces but is negligible for 95th percentile after KV warmup -> consider adjusting warmup threshold in runtime.

Quick remediation experiments (fast)
- Toggle the coalescer_backoff flag (false -> true) and replay; measure p95 delta.
- Force batches to a minimum size of 2 in canary-config and replay (fast change, safe for canary).
- Reapply PR changes with additional NVTX spans to narrow exact hot line.

Notes for bisect (if remediation experiments inconclusive)
- Bisect on the PR range: test commits around 587 (start at merge base -> PR tip). Use isolated replay scenario to evaluate each commit with a small subset of the snapshot (~5k requests).
- Keep automated bisect job timebound to 30m per commit to avoid runaway. Use 4 parallel workers to test multiple commits but ensure identical seeds.

Dashboard views to prioritize (where to look)
- route_latency.p95_by_route_and_host (6h window) -> sort by delta.
- batch_size.distribution_by_route (hourly) -> check increased micro-batches.
- runtime.span_breakdown (first_token, kv_load, forward, postprocess) -> stacked area.
- host.resource_spike_events (cpu_ss, io_wait) -> correlate.

Data collection housekeeping
- Keep all artifacts for 90 days in infra/perf/2025-01/ for audit. Archive NVTX traces and eBPF logs with names including host and timestamp.
- When sharing traces externally redact request payloads and user ids.

Decisions and next steps (current)
- 2025-01-10: revert PR 587 to canary=0% while we finish microbench suite. Owner: Maya Chen.
- 2025-01-12: run full commit-bisect across 587 range if revert does not eliminate delta. Owner: Diego Ramirez.
- 2025-01-20: follow-up to reintroduce change with more conservative backoff and NVTX instrumentation. Owner: Priya Singh.

Open questions / follow-ups
- Does the scheduler change interact with specific CPU microarch (e.g., AMD Rome vs Intel Cascade Lake) differently? Need cross-hardware runs.
- Are there background GC pauses from the Python-bridged control plane that line up with spike windows? Add GC tracing for next replay.
- Should we add a p95 SLA alert that is sensitive to small relative deltas over rolling median? Thresholding discussion needed in SRE.

Appendix: quick checklist for handing to on-call SRE
- Link to canary revert runbook: confluence.redwood.ai/INF/canary-revert (internal).
- Key commands: ps aux | grep runtime; sudo journalctl -u runtime -f; ./tools/replay --help.
- Who to page: eng-serving-runtime on-call, and Maya Chen (owner).

-- end notebook entry --
